Why split. The supplied proof B0–B10 chains four different theories. Each has a clean frozen interface and is reusable on its own:
- GMT structure off the vertex (B0.1, B1–B4, B10b): offvertex_rep. Its local step B2 (density one at a regular point forces multiplicity one, for any open U and any current) is split off as density_one_local_rep.
- Minimality ⇒ area comparison (B5a–B5d): area_comparison, for any minimizing current that is a multiplicity-one oriented C¹ piece on an open V.
- The geometric core, with no currents (B5e–B9): hypercone_plane. It covers first and second variation, Allard–Schauder smoothness, stability B.1, Simons' identity B.8, Lemma B.11, the printed proof of B.2 and the hyperplane step.
- The measure of an m-disc (B10c): subspace_ball_measure.

The sibling oriented_piece_mass. The supplied proof uses oriented_piece_mass (Submission.codim1_massOn_eq_lintegral_of_oriented_rep) in B2c, B3d, B5d and B10c.
- It is a resolved dependency of this node, so this node's own Lean proof may use it.
- It is unaccepted and owned by another parent, so it can be neither reused as a child here nor a dependency of a child. (Runtime _existing_lean_name_problem rejects the name; a child's worktree only receives its own depends_on.)
Every use is therefore routed into this node's glue or replaced, and each child proof states its departure:
- B2c–B2d: density_one_local_rep needs only a lower mass bound, from constant-covector test forms.
- B3d: offvertex_rep proves finiteness near 0 by cone scaling.
- B5d: area_comparison takes H^m(M ∩ W) ≤ M_W(C) as a hypothesis, supplied by the glue from oriented_piece_mass; for the competitor it needs only an elementary upper bound.
- B10c: the glue computes M_{B_ρ(0)}(C) from oriented_piece_mass and subspace_ball_measure.

Glue (this node's proof; Lean-checked as above). Given P, m, C, A₀ and θ with Θ^m(μ_C, 0) = θ:
1. offvertex_rep applies (1 ≤ m; C is integer multiplicity by IsMinimizingIn). It gives ξ such that M := spt C ∖ {0} is an embedded C¹ cone oriented by ξ, H^m(M ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K, and C(ω) = ∫_M ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dH^m for all ω.
2. oriented_piece_mass applies with U = V = ℝ^P, M' := M, θ' ≡ 1 and ξ' := ξ. M is Borel since spt C is closed, and ξ is a.e. strongly measurable by continuity on M. It gives M_W(C) = H^m(M ∩ W) for open W with H^m(M ∩ W) < ∞.
3. If M = ∅, every M_{B_ρ(0)}(C) = 0, so the density limit is 0 and θ = 0 ≤ 1.
4. If M ≠ ∅:
 - area_comparison with V := ℝ^P ∖ {0} gives the deformation hypothesis;
 - hypercone_plane applies (M ⊆ spt C ⊆ A₀; closure M ⊆ spt C = M ∪ {0}) and gives M = H₀ ∖ {0} with dim H₀ = m;
 - H^m{0} = 0 (m ≥ 1) and subspace_ball_measure give M_{B_ρ(0)}(C) = ω_mρ^m, so the ratio is ≡ 1 and θ = 1 ≤ 1 by uniqueness of limits.
B10a (constant orientation) is no longer needed, because oriented_piece_mass allows a non-constant measurable orientation.

Granularity.
- hypercone_plane is the largest child. Its natural internal interfaces need differential-geometric vocabulary that the contract and SimonGMT lack: C^∞ regularity, |A|, Δ_M and the stability inequality. SimonGMT has only the pointwise algebra of Appendix B and Ch. 2 §4. Freezing those interfaces belongs to its own session, which can split it (stationary and C^∞ via Allard–Schauder; B.1; B.2 for smooth stable cones; |A| ≡ 0 ⇒ plane) and reuse the Allard nodes if accepted.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Parent step B2 (B2a–B2e: local structure of M at a regular point of density one) of the supplied proof of codim1_simons_regular_cone_density, written for an arbitrary open U. Book: Simon 7.4.1 (reg T; contract regularSet), Ch. 3, 1.8(2) (density of a set with a tangent plane, chapter-03.txt lines 298–316), Ch. 6, 2.5 (M_W, chapter-06.txt line 231) and 2.11 (spt T, line 299); Ch. 2, §4, 4.1 (local representations, chapter-02.txt line 854).
Departure from the parent text, stated explicitly. The parent's B2c–B2d get M_W(T) = |m_y|·H^m(M_y ∩ W) from oriented_piece_mass. That declaration is a sibling of the parent node: it is unaccepted and owned by another parent, so it cannot be a dependency of this node. The proof below needs only a lower bound for M_{B_s(y)}(T) (step 4), obtained by testing T with one constant covector times a bump function. Membership of M_y ∩ B_ρ(y) in spt T (the last bullet of B2d) is shown in step 6b by positivity of T on such forms, not through densities.

Reused accepted declarations (sibling subproblems with identical frozen types):
- unit_orientation_dual (Submission.dor_ims_unitOrientation_dual): there is a continuous linear L : Λ_m(ℝ^P) → Λ^m(ℝ^P) such that every unit orientation ξ of a subspace satisfies (a) |ξ(α)| ≤ |α| for all α, (b) |L(ξ)| ≤ 1, (c) ξ(L(ξ)) = 1.
- chart_tangent_space (Submission.chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv): if (V, W, ψ) satisfies the chart clauses of IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r d N with r ≥ 1, then tangentSpace N (ψ v) = range Dψ(v) for every v ∈ V.
- bilipschitz_measure (Submission.dimred_rpd_bilipschitz_image_measure): if E ⊆ ℝ^n, c₁ > 0, c₂ ≥ 0 and c₁|a − b| ≤ |χ(a) − χ(b)| ≤ c₂|a − b| for a, b ∈ E, then c₁ⁿ·Lⁿ(E) ≤ Hⁿ(χ(E)) ≤ c₂ⁿ·Lⁿ(E).

Notation.
- H^m := μHE[m]. On ℝ^m = Euclid m it is Lebesgue measure L^m, and it is invariant under isometries.
- ω_m := unitBallVolume m = L^m(B_1(0)) ∈ (0, ∞), so L^m(B_r(0)) = ω_m r^m. B_s(x) := ball x s.
- Λ^m := Covector (Euclid P) m and Λ_m := MultiVector P m. ⟨α, ξ⟩ := ξ(α). |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α, a norm on Λ^m.
- M_W(T) := T.massOn W = sup{ofReal T(ω) : ω ∈ 𝒟^m(U), tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x}. Such ω are admissible for W.
- T vanishes on W if T(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W. Z(T) is the union of the open W with closure W compact and contained in U on which T vanishes; spt T = U ∖ Z(T).
- A chart of an embedded C¹ m-submanifold N at w is a triple (V, W, ψ) as in the definition of IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m N with w ∈ W.

Facts on embedded C¹ submanifolds (N an embedded C¹ m-submanifold of ℝ^P).
(F1) Charts are closed embeddings. Let (V, W, ψ) be a chart of N.
 (i) If v_j ∈ V and ψ(v_j) → z ∈ W, then a subsequence of (v_j) converges to some v ∈ V with ψ(v) = z. Indeed K := {z} ∪ {ψ(v_j) : j} is a compact subset of W, so V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact and contains every v_j; a subsequence converges in it, and ψ(v) = z by continuity of ψ on the open set V.
 (ii) Hence W ∩ N = ψ(V) is closed in W, and ψ⁻¹ : W ∩ N → V is continuous: if ψ(v_j) → ψ(v), every subsequence of (v_j) has a further subsequence converging to some v' with ψ(v') = ψ(v), and v' = v by injectivity. So ψ(V') is relatively open in N for every open V' ⊆ V.
(F0) N is Borel. By (F1)(ii) every w ∈ N has an open W_w ∋ w with W_w ∩ N closed in W_w. By second countability countably many W_{w_k} cover N, and N = ⋃_k (W_{w_k} ∩ N) is a countable union of intersections of an open and a closed set.
(F2) Open pieces. Let O ⊆ ℝ^P be open. Then N ∩ O is an embedded C¹ m-submanifold, and for w ∈ N ∩ O, tangentSpace(N ∩ O, w) = tangentSpace(N, w) = range Dψ(ψ⁻¹(w)) for every chart (V, W, ψ) of N at w. This is an m-dimensional linear subspace.
 Proof. (V ∩ ψ⁻¹(O), W ∩ O, ψ) is a chart of N ∩ O at w:
 - V ∩ ψ⁻¹(O) is open, since ψ is continuous on the open set V;
 - ψ(V ∩ ψ⁻¹(O)) = W ∩ O ∩ N;
 - for compact K ⊆ W ∩ O, (V ∩ ψ⁻¹(O)) ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) = V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact;
 - C¹-smoothness, injectivity and injectivity of Dψ restrict.
 Both charts have the same derivative at ψ⁻¹(w), so chart_tangent_space gives both tangent-space identities. range Dψ(ψ⁻¹(w)) has dimension m because Dψ(ψ⁻¹(w)) is injective on ℝ^m.
(F3) Positivity. For w ∈ N and r > 0, H^m(N ∩ B_r(w)) > 0.
 Proof. Let (V, W, ψ) be a chart at w, v₀ := ψ⁻¹(w) and A := Dψ(v₀). A is injective, so 2c|a| ≤ |Aa| for some c > 0. By continuity of Dψ choose δ > 0 with closedBall(v₀, δ) ⊆ V, ‖Dψ(v) − A‖ ≤ c on B_δ(v₀), and ψ(B_δ(v₀)) ⊆ B_r(w). For a, b ∈ B_δ(v₀) the mean value inequality for ψ − A gives |ψ(a) − ψ(b) − A(a − b)| ≤ c|a − b|. Hence c|a − b| ≤ |ψ(a) − ψ(b)| ≤ (‖A‖ + c)|a − b|. By bilipschitz_measure, H^m(ψ(B_δ(v₀))) ≥ c^m·L^m(B_δ(v₀)) > 0, and ψ(B_δ(v₀)) ⊆ N ∩ B_r(w).
(F4) Density one (Simon Ch. 3, 1.8(2), C¹ case). For w ∈ N, H^m(N ∩ B_s(w))/(ω_m s^m) → 1 as s ↓ 0.
 Proof. Set-up.
 - Let (V, W, ψ) be a chart at w, v₀ := ψ⁻¹(w), A := Dψ(v₀) and Q := range A (dimension m).
 - Let p be the orthogonal projection onto Q, p^⊥ := id − p, and ι : ℝ^m → ℝ^P a linear isometry with range Q.
 - F := ι⁻¹∘p∘(ψ − w) : V → ℝ^m is C¹ with DF(v₀) = ι⁻¹∘A invertible. By the inverse function theorem there are open V₁ ∋ v₀ (V₁ ⊆ V) and G ∋ 0 such that F : V₁ → G is a C¹ diffeomorphism.
 - Put u := p^⊥∘(ψ − w)∘F⁻¹ : G → Q^⊥ and g(a) := w + ι(a) + u(a). Then ψ∘F⁻¹ = g on G, u is C¹, u(0) = 0, and Du(0) = 0 because A has range Q.
 - By (F1)(ii), ψ(V₁) = N ∩ O₁ for an open O₁ ∋ w. Choose s₁ > 0 with B_{s₁}(w) ⊆ O₁ and closedBall(0, s₁) ⊆ G.
 - For 0 < s < s₁ put L(s) := sup{‖Du(a)‖ : |a| ≤ s}. Then L(s) → 0 as s ↓ 0.
 Estimates for 0 < s < s₁.
 - For |a|, |b| ≤ s: ι(a) − ι(b) ∈ Q is orthogonal to u(a) − u(b) ∈ Q^⊥, and |u(a) − u(b)| ≤ L(s)|a − b|. So |a − b| ≤ |g(a) − g(b)| ≤ (1 + L(s))|a − b|, and |u(a)| ≤ L(s)|a|.
 - N ∩ B_s(w) = g(E_s) with E_s := {a ∈ B_s(0) : |a|² + |u(a)|² < s²}. A point of N ∩ B_s(w) lies in ψ(V₁) = g(G), and |g(a) − w|² = |a|² + |u(a)|², which forces a ∈ E_s. Conversely g(E_s) ⊆ ψ(V₁) ⊆ N.
 - B_{s/√(1+L(s)²)}(0) ⊆ E_s ⊆ B_s(0).
 - bilipschitz_measure (χ := g, E := E_s, c₁ = 1, c₂ = 1 + L(s)) gives L^m(E_s) ≤ H^m(N ∩ B_s(w)) ≤ (1 + L(s))^m L^m(E_s).
 - Hence (1 + L(s)²)^{−m/2} ≤ H^m(N ∩ B_s(w))/(ω_m s^m) ≤ (1 + L(s))^m, and both bounds tend to 1.

Proof.
1. (Unfolding y ∈ reg T.) The definition of regularSet gives:
 - ρ_y > 0 with B_{ρ_y}(y) ⊆ U, and m_y ∈ ℤ ∖ {0};
 - an embedded C¹ m-submanifold M_y ∋ y with an orientation ξ_y: ξ_y is continuous on M_y, and for each w ∈ M_y, ξ_y(w) is a unit orientation of a subspace Q_w with (Q_w : Set) = tangentSpace(M_y, w);
 - H^m(M_y ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ B_{ρ_y}(y);
 - (R) T(ω) = m_y ∫_{M_y} ⟨ω(x), ξ_y(x)⟩ dH^m(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_{ρ_y}(y).
 For such ω the integrand is integrable on M_y. M_y is Borel by (F0). x ↦ ξ_y(x)(ω(x)) is continuous on M_y and vanishes off the compact set tsupport ω ⊆ B_{ρ_y}(y). It is bounded by |ω(x)| ≤ sup|ω| (unit_orientation_dual (a)), and H^m(M_y ∩ tsupport ω) < ∞.
2. (Choice of ρ₀.) Let (V, W, ψ) be a chart of M_y at y. By (F1)(ii), W ∩ M_y is closed in W. Choose ρ₀ > 0 with 2ρ₀ < ρ_y and B_{2ρ₀}(y) ⊆ W. Then:
 - B_{ρ₀}(y) ⊆ U;
 - closedBall(y, ρ₀) is a compact subset of B_{ρ_y}(y), so c₀ := H^m(M_y ∩ closedBall(y, ρ₀)) < ∞;
 - for every ρ ∈ (0, ρ₀], M_y ∩ B_ρ(y) is relatively closed in B_ρ(y).
3. (Dual covectors.) Let L be the map of unit_orientation_dual for (P, m). For w ∈ M_y, |L(ξ_y(w))| ≤ 1 and ξ_y(w)(L(ξ_y(w))) = 1. For fixed β ∈ Λ^m, x ↦ ξ_y(x)(β) is continuous on M_y, because evaluation at β is a continuous linear functional on Λ_m.
4. (|m_y| = 1.) Fix ε ∈ (0, 1). Put β₀ := L(ξ_y(y)) and β := sgn(m_y)·β₀, so |β| ≤ 1. By step 3 there is s₀ ∈ (0, ρ₀] with ξ_y(x)(β₀) ≥ 1 − ε for all x ∈ M_y ∩ B_{s₀}(y).
 Let 0 < s < s₀ and η ∈ (0, 1).
 - Choose a smooth φ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with φ = 1 on closedBall(y, (1 − η)s) and tsupport φ ⊆ B_s(y).
 - ω := φ·β is smooth with compact tsupport ω ⊆ B_s(y) ⊆ U, so ω ∈ 𝒟^m(U). Also |ω(x)| = φ(x)|β| ≤ 1, so ω is admissible for B_s(y) and ofReal(T(ω)) ≤ M_{B_s(y)}(T).
 - By (R), T(ω) = m_y·sgn(m_y) ∫_{M_y} φ·ξ_y(β₀) dH^m = |m_y| ∫_{M_y} φ(x) ξ_y(x)(β₀) dH^m(x).
 - The integrand is ≥ 0 on M_y: φ = 0 off B_s(y), and ξ_y(β₀) ≥ 1 − ε > 0 on M_y ∩ B_s(y). It is ≥ 1 − ε on M_y ∩ closedBall(y, (1 − η)s).
 - Hence M_{B_s(y)}(T) ≥ |m_y|(1 − ε)·H^m(M_y ∩ closedBall(y, (1 − η)s)).
 As η ↓ 0 the closed balls increase to B_s(y). By continuity of measure from below,
 (4.1) M_{B_s(y)}(T) ≥ |m_y|(1 − ε)·H^m(M_y ∩ B_s(y)) for 0 < s < s₀.
 Divide by ω_m s^m ∈ (0, ∞) and let s ↓ 0:
 - the left side tends to 1 by the hypothesis HasMassDensity T y 1;
 - the right side tends to |m_y|(1 − ε) by (F4) with N := M_y and w := y.
 So |m_y|(1 − ε) ≤ 1 for every ε ∈ (0, 1), and |m_y| ≤ 1. Since m_y is a nonzero integer, m_y ∈ {1, −1}.
5. (The orientation.) Put ξ(x) := m_y·ξ_y(x) = ±ξ_y(x).
 - ξ is continuous on M_y.
 - For w ∈ M_y, ξ(w) is a unit orientation of Q_w, since IsUnitOrientationOf allows either sign. Hence |L(ξ(w))| ≤ 1 and ξ(w)(L(ξ(w))) = 1.
 - (R) becomes (R') T(ω) = ∫_{M_y} ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dH^m whenever tsupport ω ⊆ B_{ρ_y}(y).
6. (Support.) Fix ρ ∈ (0, ρ₀] and put S := spt T ∩ B_ρ(y). We show S = M_y ∩ B_ρ(y).
 (6a) S ⊆ M_y. Let x ∈ B_ρ(y) ∖ M_y.

 - Put β_w := L(ξ(w)). By continuity choose r > 0 with B_r(w) ⊆ O ∩ B_ρ(y) and ξ(x)(β_w) ≥ 1/2 for x ∈ M_y ∩ B_r(w).

Departures from the parent text, stated explicitly.
(i) The parent's finiteness H^m(M ∩ B_ρ(0)) < ∞ (end of B3d) used oriented_piece_mass. That declaration is unaccepted and owned by another parent, so it cannot be a dependency here. Step 6b replaces it by a cone-scaling argument.
(ii) Agreement of the local orientations on overlaps (B3a–B3b) is proved with orientation_sign and a positive bump-form test (step 4), instead of testing against a countable dense family of covectors. The idea is the same.
(iii) The vertex is handled for every test form at once (B0.1 combined with the dominated-convergence argument of B10b, valid for any locally H^m-finite M). So the case M = ∅ (B1) needs no separate treatment: the representation then reads C = 0.

Sibling subproblems used.
- density_one_local_rep (Submission.codim1_density_one_regular_local_rep): if U is open, m ≥ 1, y ∈ reg T and Θ^m(μ_T, y) = 1, there is ρ₀ > 0 with B_{ρ₀}(y) ⊆ U such that for every ρ ∈ (0, ρ₀] there is ξ with:
 - spt T ∩ B_ρ(y) an embedded C¹ m-submanifold oriented by ξ;
 - H^m(spt T ∩ B_ρ(y)) < ∞;
 - T(ω) = ∫_{spt T ∩ B_ρ(y)} ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dH^m whenever tsupport ω ⊆ B_ρ(y).
- vanish_off_support (Submission.dtc_vanish_off_support): S(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω is disjoint from spt S.
- cone_pullback_identity (Submission.cone_current_apply_dilation_pullback): for a cone C, λ > 0 and ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) there is ω' ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with ω'(z) = λ^{−m}ω(λ^{−1}z) for all z and C(ω') = C(ω).
- unit_orientation_dual (Submission.dor_ims_unitOrientation_dual): a continuous linear L : Λ_m → Λ^m such that every unit orientation ξ of a subspace satisfies (a) |ξ(α)| ≤ |α|, (b) |L(ξ)| ≤ 1, (c) ξ(L(ξ)) = 1.
- orientation_sign (Submission.rsdic_unitOrientation_eq_or_eq_neg): two unit orientations v, w of the same subspace satisfy w = v or w = −v.
- chart_tangent_space (Submission.chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv): for a chart (V, W, ψ) of an embedded C^r submanifold N (r ≥ 1), tangentSpace N (ψ v) = range Dψ(v).
- bilipschitz_measure (Submission.dimred_rpd_bilipschitz_image_measure): if c₁|a − b| ≤ |χ(a) − χ(b)| ≤ c₂|a − b| on E ⊆ ℝ^n (c₁ > 0, c₂ ≥ 0), then c₁ⁿLⁿ(E) ≤ Hⁿ(χ(E)) ≤ c₂ⁿLⁿ(E).

Notation.
- H^m := μHE[m], B_s(x) := ball x s, ⟨α, ξ⟩ := ξ(α), |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α (a norm on Λ^m), sup|ω| := sup_x |ω(x)| < ∞ for ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P).
- "C vanishes on W" means C(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W. Z(C) is the union of the open W with compact closure on which C vanishes; spt C = ℝ^P ∖ Z(C).
- M := spt C ∖ {0}.
Facts on embedded C¹ m-submanifolds N.
(F0) N is Borel.
(F1) For a chart (V, W, ψ), W ∩ N is closed in W and ψ⁻¹ : W ∩ N → V is continuous.
(F2) For open O, N ∩ O is an embedded C¹ m-submanifold, and tangentSpace(N ∩ O, w) = tangentSpace(N, w) = range Dψ(ψ⁻¹(w)) (dimension m) for w ∈ N ∩ O and every chart (V, W, ψ) of N at w.
(F3) H^m(N ∩ B_r(w)) > 0 for w ∈ N and r > 0.
Proofs.
- (F1): if ψ(v_j) → z ∈ W, the compact set K := {z} ∪ {ψ(v_j)} ⊆ W has V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) compact; a subsequence v_j → v ∈ V with ψ(v) = z. With injectivity of ψ this gives both claims.
- (F0): by (F1) each point of N has an open W with W ∩ N relatively closed in W, and countably many such W cover N.
- (F2): (V ∩ ψ⁻¹(O), W ∩ O, ψ) is a chart of N ∩ O with the same derivative, and chart_tangent_space computes both tangent spaces.
- (F3): near v₀ := ψ⁻¹(w), ψ satisfies c|a − b| ≤ |ψ(a) − ψ(b)| ≤ C|a − b| on a small ball B_δ(v₀) mapped into B_r(w), by the mean value inequality for ψ − Dψ(v₀) and injectivity of Dψ(v₀). bilipschitz_measure then gives H^m(ψ(B_δ(v₀))) ≥ c^m L^m(B_δ(v₀)) > 0.

Proof. Fix P, m ≥ 1 and C as in the statement.
1. (Local pieces.) Let y ∈ M. Then y ∈ spt C and y ≠ 0, so by hypothesis y ∈ reg C and Θ^m(μ_C, y) = 1.
 - Apply density_one_local_rep with U := ℝ^P and T := C to get ρ₀(y). Put ρ_y := min{ρ₀(y), |y|/2} > 0, B_y := B_{ρ_y}(y), and let ξ_y be the orientation given for ρ = ρ_y.
 - Since 0 ∉ B_y, S_y := spt C ∩ B_y = M ∩ B_y.
 - Hence S_y is an embedded C¹ m-submanifold, ξ_y is an orientation of S_y, H^m(S_y) < ∞, and
 (1.1) C(ω) = ∫_{M ∩ B_y} ⟨ω, ξ_y⟩ dH^m for every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_y.
2. (M is an embedded C¹ submanifold.) Let y ∈ M and (V, W, ψ) a chart of S_y at y. Then (V, W ∩ B_y, ψ) is a chart of M at y:
 - W ∩ B_y is open and contains y;
 - ψ(V) = W ∩ S_y ⊆ B_y, so ψ(V) = (W ∩ B_y) ∩ M;
 - for compact K ⊆ W ∩ B_y, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact;
 - the remaining clauses are those of the chart of S_y.
 Hence IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 1 m M. By (F2) with N := M and O := B_y, tangentSpace(S_y, w) = tangentSpace(M, w) for w ∈ S_y. spt C is closed, as Z(C) is a union of open sets. Hence M is relatively closed in ℝ^P ∖ {0} and Borel.
3. (Cone property; parent B4.) Let t > 0 and let W be open with compact closure, with C vanishing on W.
 - Let ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ tW. cone_pullback_identity with λ := t⁻¹ gives ω' ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with ω'(z) = t^m ω(tz) and C(ω') = C(ω).
 - tsupport ω' = t⁻¹·tsupport ω ⊆ W, so C(ω) = C(ω') = 0. Thus C vanishes on tW.
 - tW is open with compact closure t·closure(W), so tW ⊆ Z(C).
 Hence t·Z(C) ⊆ Z(C) for every t > 0. Applying this to t⁻¹ gives t·Z(C) = Z(C), so t·spt C = spt C. As tx ≠ 0 for x ≠ 0, tx ∈ M for every x ∈ M and t > 0.
4. (Agreement on overlaps.) Let y, y' ∈ M and G := M ∩ B_y ∩ B_{y'}. We show ξ_{y'} = ξ_y on G.
 - For w ∈ G, ξ_y(w) and ξ_{y'}(w) are unit orientations of subspaces whose carrier is tangentSpace(M, w) (step 2), hence of the same subspace (a submodule is determined by its carrier). By orientation_sign, ξ_{y'}(w) = ±ξ_y(w).
 - Suppose ξ_{y'}(w₀) = −ξ_y(w₀) for some w₀ ∈ G. As ξ_y(w₀)(L(ξ_y(w₀))) = 1, ξ_y(w₀) ≠ 0, so ξ_{y'}(w₀) ≠ ξ_y(w₀).
 - By continuity of ξ_y and ξ_{y'} on G, choose r > 0 with B_r(w₀) ⊆ B_y ∩ B_{y'} such that, with β := L(ξ_y(w₀)), for every x ∈ M ∩ B_r(w₀): ξ_{y'}(x) ≠ ξ_y(x), hence ξ_{y'}(x) = −ξ_y(x); and ξ_y(x)(β) ≥ 1/2.
 - Take a smooth φ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with φ = 1 on closedBall(w₀, r/2) and tsupport φ ⊆ B_r(w₀), and ω := φ·β.
 - By (1.1) for y and for y', C(ω) = ∫_M φ·ξ_y(β) dH^m = ∫_M φ·ξ_{y'}(β) dH^m = −∫_M φ·ξ_y(β) dH^m. So ∫_M φ·ξ_y(β) dH^m = 0.
 - But this integrand is ≥ 0, and ≥ 1/2 on M ∩ B_{r/2}(w₀), which has positive H^m-measure by (F3) (step 2).
 This contradiction shows ξ_{y'} = ξ_y on G.
5. (Global orientation.) Define ξ_M(x) := ξ_x(x) for x ∈ M and ξ_M(x) := 0 for x ∉ M.
 - For y ∈ M and x ∈ M ∩ B_y, step 4 (with y' := x, using x ∈ B_x) gives ξ_M(x) = ξ_x(x) = ξ_y(x). So ξ_M = ξ_y on the relatively open set M ∩ B_y ∋ y.
 - Hence ξ_M is continuous on M, since ξ_y is continuous on S_y = M ∩ B_y.
 - For x ∈ M, ξ_M(x) = ξ_x(x) is a unit orientation of a subspace with carrier tangentSpace(S_x, x) = tangentSpace(M, x) (step 2).
 Thus IsOrientation m M ξ_M.
6. (Local finiteness.)
 (6a) Let K be compact with 0 ∉ K. Then M ∩ K = spt C ∩ K is compact and covered by the open balls B_y (y ∈ M ∩ K), hence by finitely many B_{y_1}, …, B_{y_N}. So H^m(M ∩ K) ≤ Σ_j H^m(S_{y_j}) < ∞.
 (6b) Let R > 0 and A := {x : R/2 ≤ |x| ≤ R}, a compact set with 0 ∉ A, so a := H^m(M ∩ A) < ∞ by (6a).
 - If x ∈ M and |x| ≤ R, then x ≠ 0 and there is k ∈ ℕ with R·2^{−k−1} ≤ |x| ≤ R·2^{−k}. By step 3, 2^k x ∈ M ∩ A, i.e. x ∈ 2^{−k}·(M ∩ A).
 - So M ∩ closedBall(0, R) ⊆ ⋃_{k≥0} 2^{−k}·(M ∩ A).
 - By countable subadditivity and the scaling law H^m(λE) = λ^m H^m(E) for λ > 0 (Mathlib Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀), H^m(M ∩ closedBall(0, R)) ≤ Σ_{k≥0} 2^{−km} a = a/(1 − 2^{−m}) < ∞, because m ≥ 1.
 (6c) Every compact K lies in some closedBall(0, R), so H^m(M ∩ K) < ∞.
7. (Representation off the vertex; parent B3c.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with 0 ∉ tsupport ω. We show C(ω) = ∫_M ⟨ω, ξ_M⟩ dH^m.
 - K := tsupport ω is compact. Each x ∈ K lies in B_x (if x ∈ spt C; then x ∈ M since x ≠ 0) or in the open set O₀ := ℝ^P ∖ spt C.
 - Choose y_1, …, y_N ∈ M with K ⊆ O₀ ∪ B_{y_1} ∪ ⋯ ∪ B_{y_N}, and smooth compactly supported φ_0, …, φ_N with tsupport φ_0 ⊆ O₀, tsupport φ_j ⊆ B_{y_j} for j ≥ 1, and Σ_j φ_j = 1 on K (smooth partition of unity subordinate to this finite cover). Then ω = Σ_j φ_jω with φ_jω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P).
 - For j ≥ 1, by (1.1) and step 5: C(φ_jω) = ∫_{M ∩ B_{y_j}} ⟨φ_jω, ξ_{y_j}⟩ dH^m = ∫_M ⟨φ_jω, ξ_M⟩ dH^m. The integrand vanishes off B_{y_j}, and ξ_{y_j} = ξ_M on M ∩ B_{y_j}.
 - For j = 0, tsupport(φ_0ω) ⊆ O₀ is disjoint from spt C, so C(φ_0ω) = 0 by vanish_off_support. Also φ_0 = 0 on spt C ⊇ M, so ∫_M ⟨φ_0ω, ξ_M⟩ dH^m = 0.
 - All integrands are measurable (continuous on the Borel set M) and bounded by sup|ω|·1_K (unit_orientation_dual (a)), and H^m(M ∩ K) < ∞ (step 6). So they are integrable, and summing over j by linearity gives the claim.
8. (Vertex negligibility; parent B0.1.) C is integer multiplicity; fix an IMRep R = (M_R, θ_R, ξ_R) of C. For ε ∈ (0, 1/2] fix a smooth χ_ε : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with χ_ε = 1 on B_ε(0) and tsupport χ_ε ⊆ B_{2ε}(0). Let ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P). Then C(χ_εω) = ∫_{M_R} θ_R·χ_ε·ξ_R(ω) dH^m → 0 as ε ↓ 0. Here and in step 9, "as ε ↓ 0" means along every sequence ε_k ↓ 0 (equivalently along the countably generated filter 𝓝[>]0), so the sequential dominated convergence theorem applies:
 - by R.orients and unit_orientation_dual (a), |ξ_R(x)(ω(x))| ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ sup|ω| for H^m-a.e. x ∈ M_R;
 - so the integrand is dominated by θ_R·sup|ω|·1_{closedBall(0,1)}, which is integrable on M_R because ∫_{M_R ∩ closedBall(0,1)} θ_R dH^m < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult);
 - pointwise, χ_ε(x) → 0 for x ≠ 0 (χ_ε(x) = 0 once 2ε ≤ |x|), and H^m({0}) = 0 because m ≥ 1;
 - dominated convergence gives the limit 0.
 Since C(ω) = C(χ_εω) + C((1 − χ_ε)ω), it follows that C(ω) = lim_{ε↓0} C((1 − χ_ε)ω).
9. (Global representation; parent B10b.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P).
 - (1 − χ_ε)ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) vanishes on B_ε(0), so 0 ∉ tsupport((1 − χ_ε)ω). Step 7 gives C((1 − χ_ε)ω) = ∫_M (1 − χ_ε)⟨ω, ξ_M⟩ dH^m.
 - These integrands are dominated by sup|ω|·1_{tsupport ω}, integrable on M by step 6. They converge pointwise on M to ⟨ω, ξ_M⟩, because 0 ∉ M.
 - By dominated convergence along any sequence ε_k ↓ 0, and step 8, C(ω) = ∫_M ⟨ω(x), ξ_M(x)⟩ dH^m(x).
10. Steps 2, 5, 3, 6 and 9 are the five conclusions, with ξ := ξ_M. (If M = ∅ they hold trivially, and step 9 says C = 0.) ∎

Book: Simon 7.1.1 (minimizing); Appendix B, chapter-B.txt lines 13–23 ("H^n(M_t) takes its minimum value at t = 0, by virtue of our assumption that C is minimizing"); Ch. 6, 1.13–1.14 (pull-back of forms, d∘f^# = f^#∘d; chapter-06.txt lines 153–168), 2.23–2.24 (push-forward f_#T(ω) = T(f^#ω), ∂f_#T = f_#∂T, and the formula for f_#[[M]]; lines 403–440) and 3.3–3.9 (push-forward of integer multiplicity currents; lines 778–859); Ch. 2, §5, 5.1–5.2 (the area formula for φ_t(M ∩ K); chapter-02.txt lines 1162–1205).
Departure from the parent text, stated explicitly. The parent proved M_W(C) = H^m(M ∩ W) and M_W(S_t) = H^m(Φ_t(M ∩ W)) with oriented_piece_mass, which this node cannot depend on (unaccepted, owned by another parent). Here:
- the lower bound for C is the hypothesis (H_mass), which the parent node derives from oriented_piece_mass;

Sibling subproblems used.
- unit_orientation_dual (Submission.dor_ims_unitOrientation_dual): every unit orientation η of a subspace satisfies |η(α)| ≤ |α| for every m-covector α.
- chart_tangent_space (Submission.chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv): for a chart (V, W, ψ) of an embedded C^r submanifold (r ≥ 1), tangentSpace N (ψ v) = range Dψ(v). In particular each T_xM := tangentSpace(M, x), x ∈ M, is an m-dimensional linear subspace.

Notation and hypotheses.
- H^m := μHE[m]; ⟨α, ξ⟩ := ξ(α); |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; M_W(T) := T.massOn W.
- For a linear map A and an m-covector α, α∘A is the covector (v_1, …, v_m) ↦ α(Av_1, …, Av_m).
- For ξ ∈ Λ_m, Λ_mA ξ is the m-vector α ↦ ξ(α∘A).
- The data are P, m ≥ 1 and C ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) minimizing in ℝ^P with ∂C = 0. V is open, and M ⊆ V is an embedded C¹ m-submanifold with orientation ξ. Hypotheses:
 (LF) H^m(M ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ V;
 (Rep) C(ω) = ∫_M ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dH^m(x) whenever tsupport ω ⊆ V;
 (H_mass) H^m(M ∩ W) ≤ M_W(C) for every open W ⊆ V with H^m(M ∩ W) < ∞.
- Z : ℝ^P → ℝ^P is C^∞ with compact support and K := tsupport Z ⊆ V. Put Φ_t(x) := x + tZ(x).
(F0) M is Borel. For a chart (V', W', ψ) of M, W' ∩ M is closed in W' (if ψ(v_j) → z ∈ W', the compact set {z} ∪ {ψ(v_j)} ⊆ W' has compact preimage in V', so a subsequence v_j → v with ψ(v) = z). Countably many such W' cover M.

Proof.
1. (Constants and the open set W.)
 - If K = ∅ then Z = 0, Φ_t = id for all t, and the claim holds with t₀ := 1. Assume K ≠ ∅ from now on.
 - K is compact and K ⊆ V. Let δ := ½·dist(K, ℝ^P ∖ V) > 0 (δ := 1 if V = ℝ^P) and W := {x : dist(x, K) < δ}.
 - W is open, K ⊆ W, and closure(W) ⊆ {x : dist(x, K) ≤ δ} is a compact subset of V. By (LF), H^m(M ∩ closure W) < ∞.
 - Let Λ := sup_x ‖DZ(x)‖ < ∞ and t₀ := 1/(1 + Λ) > 0. Fix t with |t| < t₀ and write Φ := Φ_t.
2. (Φ is a C^∞ diffeomorphism of ℝ^P with Φ = id off K, Φ(K) = K, Φ(W) = W, Φ(V) = V.)
 - Φ is C^∞ and DΦ(x) = I + tDZ(x) with ‖tDZ(x)‖ ≤ |t|Λ < 1, so DΦ(x) is invertible.
 - By the mean value inequality |Z(a) − Z(b)| ≤ Λ|a − b|. Hence (1 − |t|Λ)|a − b| ≤ |Φ(a) − Φ(b)| ≤ (1 + |t|Λ)|a − b|, and Φ is injective.
 - Φ is surjective: for y ∈ ℝ^P, x ↦ y − tZ(x) is a contraction of ℝ^P with constant |t|Λ < 1, and its fixed point x satisfies Φ(x) = y.
 - By the inverse function theorem Φ⁻¹ is C^∞, and Φ is proper.
 - Z = 0 on the open set ℝ^P ∖ K, so Φ = id there. A bijection fixing every point of ℝ^P ∖ K maps K onto K. Hence Φ(W) = W and Φ(V) = V.
3. (The competitor S := Φ_#C; Simon 6.2.23.) For ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) let (Φ^#ω)(x) := ω(Φ(x))∘DΦ(x) (Simon 6.1.13).
 - Φ^#ω is C^∞ with tsupport Φ^#ω ⊆ Φ⁻¹(tsupport ω), which is compact. So Φ^#ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P), and ω ↦ Φ^#ω is linear.
 - If ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) (supports in a fixed compact K', all derivatives → 0 uniformly), then Φ^#ω_j → 0 in 𝒟^m(ℝ^P): the supports lie in the compact Φ⁻¹(K'), and by the chain and Leibniz rules all derivatives → 0 uniformly, since every derivative of Φ is bounded on compact sets.
 Hence S(ω) := C(Φ^#ω) defines S ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P).
4. (S is an admissible competitor.)
 (4a) Integer multiplicity. By the first conjunct of IsMinimizingIn, C = τ(M_R, θ_R, ξ_R) for an IMRep R. Φ is Lipschitz, injective and proper, so S = Φ_#C is integer multiplicity by Simon 6.3.9:
 - S = τ(Φ(M_R), θ_R∘Φ⁻¹, ξ_S) with ξ_S(Φ(x)) = Λ_mDΦ(x)ξ_R(x)/|Λ_mDΦ(x)ξ_R(x)| (6.3.3–6.3.8; N = θ_R∘Φ⁻¹ because Φ is injective);
 - Φ(M_R) is Borel (Φ is a homeomorphism) and countably m-rectifiable;
 - its approximate tangent space at Φ(x) is DΦ(x)(T_xM_R) for H^m-a.e. x ∈ M_R;
 - θ_R∘Φ⁻¹ is locally H^m-integrable: by the area formula, for compact K', ∫_{Φ(M_R)∩K'} θ_R∘Φ⁻¹ dH^m = ∫_{M_R ∩ Φ⁻¹K'} θ_R·J^{M_R}Φ dH^m ≤ (1 + |t|Λ)^m ∫_{M_R ∩ Φ⁻¹K'} θ_R dH^m < ∞.
 (4b) Same boundary. Write m = k + 1. For φ ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P), Φ^#φ ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) and d(Φ^#φ) = Φ^#(dφ) (Simon 6.1.14). So ∂S(φ) = S(dφ) = C(d(Φ^#φ)) = ∂C(Φ^#φ) = 0. Hence ∂S = 0 = ∂C, i.e. SameBoundary S C (also Simon 6.2.24(1)).
 (4c) Support of the difference. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ∩ K = ∅. Then Φ^#ω = ω:
 - at x ∉ K, Φ = id on the open neighbourhood ℝ^P ∖ K of x, so Φ(x) = x and DΦ(x) = I;
 - at x ∈ K, Φ(x) ∈ K, so ω(Φ(x)) = 0 = ω(x).
 Hence (S − C)(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ K. Every x ∉ K has a ball with closure in ℝ^P ∖ K on which S − C vanishes, so spt(S − C) ⊆ K. Thus spt(S − C) is a closed subset of K, hence compact, and spt(S − C) ⊆ ℝ^P ∩ W.
 (4d) Minimality. W is open and CompactlyContained W ℝ^P (closure W is compact). The second conjunct of IsMinimizingIn C univ gives
 (4.1) M_W(C) ≤ M_W(S).
5. (Lower bound for C.) W ⊆ V is open and H^m(M ∩ W) ≤ H^m(M ∩ closure W) < ∞. By (H_mass), H^m(M ∩ W) ≤ M_W(C).
6. (Upper bound for S.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x.
 - tsupport Φ^#ω ⊆ Φ⁻¹(W) = W ⊆ V. By (Rep), S(ω) = C(Φ^#ω) = ∫_M ⟨ω(Φ(x))∘DΦ(x), ξ(x)⟩ dH^m(x) = ∫_M ⟨ω(Φ(x)), Λ_mDΦ(x)ξ(x)⟩ dH^m(x).
 - Pointwise bound. Fix x ∈ M. Since ξ is an orientation of M, ξ(x)(β) = ±β(τ_1, …, τ_m) for all β, where τ_1, …, τ_m is an orthonormal basis of T_xM. Put v_i := DΦ(x)τ_i; they are linearly independent and span Q' := DΦ(x)(T_xM). Let J(x) := √det(v_i·v_j) > 0; this is the Jacobian J^MΦ(x) of Φ|_M (Simon Ch. 2, §3). Gram–Schmidt gives an orthonormal basis e_1, …, e_m of Q' and a triangular matrix G with v = e·G and |det G| = J(x). So α(v_1, …, v_m) = det G·α(e_1, …, e_m) for every α. Hence ⟨α, Λ_mDΦ(x)ξ(x)⟩ = J(x)·η(α), where η(α) := ±sgn(det G)·α(e_1, …, e_m) is a unit orientation of Q'. By unit_orientation_dual (a), |⟨α, Λ_mDΦ(x)ξ(x)⟩| ≤ J(x)|α|.
 - With α := ω(Φ(x)): |α| ≤ 1, and α = 0 unless Φ(x) ∈ W, i.e. unless x ∈ Φ⁻¹(W) = W. Hence |S(ω)| ≤ ∫_{M∩W} J^MΦ dH^m.
 - Area formula for the injective C¹ map Φ on the C¹ submanifold M (Simon Ch. 2, §3 and 5.1–5.2; cf. 6.2.24(3)): ∫_{M∩W} J^MΦ dH^m = H^m(Φ(M ∩ W)) ≤ (1 + |t|Λ)^m H^m(M ∩ W) < ∞.
 Taking the supremum over such ω:
 (6.1) M_W(S) ≤ H^m(Φ(M ∩ W)).
7. (Localization to K.) Steps 4–6 give H^m(M ∩ W) ≤ M_W(C) ≤ M_W(S) ≤ H^m(Φ(M ∩ W)). Now:
 - M ∩ W is the disjoint union of M ∩ K and M ∩ (W ∖ K);
 - Φ(M ∩ W) is the disjoint union of Φ(M ∩ K) ⊆ K and Φ(M ∩ (W ∖ K)) = M ∩ (W ∖ K), since Φ = id off K;
 - all four sets are Borel (M is Borel by (F0), K is closed, Φ is a homeomorphism).
 With b := H^m(M ∩ (W ∖ K)) ≤ H^m(M ∩ closure W) < ∞ this reads H^m(M ∩ K) + b ≤ H^m(Φ(M ∩ K)) + b. Hence H^m(M ∩ tsupport Z) ≤ H^m((x ↦ x + tZ(x))(M ∩ tsupport Z)).
8. Step 7 holds for every t with |t| < t₀, and t₀ > 0. This is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: For |t| < 1/(1 + sup‖DZ‖), Φ_t = id + tZ is a C^∞ diffeomorphism equal to id off K = tsupport Z, with Φ_t(K) = K and Φ_t(W) = W for an open W ⊇ K whose closure is a compact subset of V.
S_t = Φ_{t#}C is integer multiplicity (Simon 6.3.9), ∂S_t = Φ_{t#}∂C = 0 and spt(S_t − C) ⊆ K. Minimality gives M_W(C) ≤ M_W(S_t).
M_W(C) ≥ H^m(M ∩ W) by hypothesis. M_W(S_t) ≤ H^m(Φ_t(M ∩ W)) by the representation, |⟨α, Λ_mDΦ_tξ⟩| ≤ J^MΦ_t·|α| (unit_orientation_dual) and the area formula.
Subtracting the finite common part H^m(M ∩ (W ∖ K)) gives H^m(M ∩ K) ≤ H^m(Φ_t(M ∩ K)).

subproblems.title: Simons' theorem (Simon B.2) for C¹ hypercones minimizing area under deformations away from the vertex (parent B5e–B9)
subproblems.statement: Simons' theorem for deformation-minimal C¹ hypercones. Data: P, m ∈ ℕ with 2 ≤ m ≤ 6; a linear subspace A₀ ⊆ ℝ^P with dim A₀ = m + 1; M ⊆ ℝ^P. Hypotheses: M ≠ ∅, M ⊆ A₀ and 0 ∉ M; M is an embedded C¹ m-submanifold of ℝ^P; closure(M) ⊆ M ∪ {0}; tx ∈ M for every x ∈ M and t > 0; M has an orientation ξ (IsOrientation m M ξ for some ξ); H^m(M ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K; and for every C^∞ map Z : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with compact support and 0 ∉ tsupport Z there is t₀ > 0 with H^m(M ∩ tsupport Z) ≤ H^m({x + tZ(x) : x ∈ M ∩ tsupport Z}) for every t with |t| < t₀. Conclusion: there is a linear subspace H₀ ⊆ ℝ^P with dim H₀ = m and M = H₀ ∖ {0}. H^m = μHE[m].

Departures from the parent text, stated explicitly.
(i) The hypothesis (AC) below is the conclusion of the parent's B5d with the compact set K_Z := tsupport Z in place of the open set W ⊇ K_Z. This is equivalent, because Φ_t = id off K_Z.
(ii) The parent identified A₀ with ℝ^{m+1}; here everything is done inside A₀ ⊆ ℝ^P. The unit normal of M in A₀ is built from the given orientation ξ (step 3), which is exactly how B7a uses "the orientation induced from C".
(iii) The printed proof uses ε both for the cut-off parameter and for the exponent; the cut-off parameter is called κ here (as in the parent).

Sibling subproblems used.
- chart_tangent_space (Submission.chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv): for a chart (V, W, ψ) of an embedded C^r submanifold N (r ≥ 1), tangentSpace N (ψ v) = range Dψ(v).
- bilipschitz_measure (Submission.dimred_rpd_bilipschitz_image_measure): if c₁|a − b| ≤ |χ(a) − χ(b)| ≤ c₂|a − b| on E ⊆ ℝ^n (c₁ > 0, c₂ ≥ 0), then c₁ⁿLⁿ(E) ≤ Hⁿ(χ(E)) ≤ c₂ⁿLⁿ(E).

Hypotheses and notation.
- P, m with 2 ≤ m ≤ 6; A₀ ⊆ ℝ^P a linear subspace with dim A₀ = m + 1; M ⊆ A₀ nonempty with 0 ∉ M.
- M is an embedded C¹ m-submanifold, closure(M) ⊆ M ∪ {0}, and tx ∈ M for x ∈ M, t > 0.
- ξ is an orientation of M.
- (LF) H^m(M ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K.
- (AC) For every C^∞ map Z : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with compact support and 0 ∉ K_Z := tsupport Z there is t₀(Z) > 0 with H^m(M ∩ K_Z) ≤ H^m(Φ_t^Z(M ∩ K_Z)) for |t| < t₀(Z), where Φ_t^Z(x) := x + tZ(x).
- H^m := μHE[m], ω_m := unitBallVolume m, r(x) := |x|, U₀ := ℝ^P ∖ {0}, B_s(x) := ball x s.

Facts on embedded C¹ m-submanifolds N (proofs as indicated).
(F1) For a chart (V, W, ψ) of N, W ∩ N is closed in W and ψ⁻¹ : W ∩ N → V is continuous. If ψ(v_j) → z ∈ W, the compact set {z} ∪ {ψ(v_j)} ⊆ W has compact preimage in V; a subsequence v_j → v with ψ(v) = z, and injectivity gives continuity of ψ⁻¹. Consequently N is Borel: countably many such W cover N.
(F2) For x ∈ N, T_xN := tangentSpace(N, x) = range Dψ(ψ⁻¹(x)) for any chart (chart_tangent_space). It is an m-dimensional linear subspace, and the same holds for N ∩ O, O open, with the same tangent spaces (restrict the chart to V ∩ ψ⁻¹(O)).
(F3) H^m(N ∩ B_s(x)) > 0 for x ∈ N, s > 0. Near v₀ := ψ⁻¹(x), ψ is bi-Lipschitz on a small ball mapped into B_s(x) (mean value inequality and injectivity of Dψ(v₀)); apply bilipschitz_measure.
(F4) H^m(N ∩ B_s(x))/(ω_m s^m) → 1 as s ↓ 0 (Simon Ch. 3, 1.8(2)). Near x, N is the graph {x + a + u(a)} over T_xN (identified isometrically with ℝ^m) of a C¹ map u with u(0) = 0, Du(0) = 0. This follows from the inverse function theorem applied to the projection onto T_xN of ψ − x, and (F1). With L(s) := sup_{|a|≤s}‖Du(a)‖ → 0, the graph map g is bi-Lipschitz on B_s(0) with constants 1 and 1 + L(s). Also N ∩ B_s(x) = g(E_s) with B_{s/√(1+L(s)²)}(0) ⊆ E_s ⊆ B_s(0). bilipschitz_measure gives (1 + L(s)²)^{−m/2} ≤ H^m(N ∩ B_s(x))/(ω_m s^m) ≤ (1 + L(s))^m.

Proof.
0. (Preliminaries.)
 (0a) Cone and closure. Applying the cone hypothesis with t and t⁻¹ gives tM = M for t > 0. For x ∈ M, tx → 0 as t ↓ 0, so 0 ∈ closure(M); with closure(M) ⊆ M ∪ {0} and 0 ∉ M, closure(M) ∖ M = {0}. Hence M is relatively closed in U₀ and Borel (F1).
 (0b) Tangent spaces. For x ∈ M, T_xM is m-dimensional (F2), and T_xM ⊆ A₀: a C¹ curve in M ⊆ A₀ has its derivative in the closed subspace A₀. Also x ∈ T_xM: s ↦ e^s x is a C¹ curve in M with derivative x at 0. Hence the radial unit vector x/|x| is tangent and |∇^M r| = 1 on M.
 (0c) Area formula for the variations (Simon Ch. 2, 5.1–5.2). Let Z be as in (AC) and Λ := sup‖DZ‖. For |t| < 1/(1 + Λ), Φ_t := Φ_t^Z is a C^∞ diffeomorphism of ℝ^P: DΦ_t = I + tDZ is invertible, |Φ_t(a) − Φ_t(b)| ≥ (1 − |t|Λ)|a − b|, and Φ_t is onto by the contraction argument. Φ_t = id off K_Z and Φ_t(K_Z) = K_Z. By the area formula for the injective C¹ map Φ_t on M,
 f_Z(t) := H^m(Φ_t(M ∩ K_Z)) = ∫_{M∩K_Z} J_t dH^m,
 where J_t(x) := √det G_t(x), G_t(x)_{ij} := (τ_i + tDZ(x)τ_i)·(τ_j + tDZ(x)τ_j), and τ is an orthonormal basis of T_xM.
1. (First variation and stationarity; parent B5e.) Let Z be as in (AC).
 - det G_t(x) is a polynomial in t whose coefficients are bounded on M ∩ K_Z by constants depending only on m and Λ, and G_0 = I. So there is t₁ ∈ (0, 1/(1 + Λ)) with det G_t ≥ 1/2 for |t| ≤ t₁. For such t, Φ_t is a diffeomorphism and the area-formula expression (0c) for f_Z(t) is valid.
 - Hence J_t is C^∞ in t, with |∂_t^k J_t(x)| ≤ C_k for x ∈ M ∩ K_Z and |t| ≤ t₁.
 - Since H^m(M ∩ K_Z) < ∞ by (LF), f_Z is C^∞ on (−t₁, t₁) and may be differentiated under the integral. ∂_tJ_t|_{t=0} = Σ_i τ_i·DZ(x)τ_i = div_M Z(x) (Simon 5.2–5.3).
 - By (AC), f_Z(t) ≥ f_Z(0) for |t| < min{t₀(Z), t₁}, so f_Z has a local minimum at 0: f_Z'(0) = 0 and f_Z''(0) ≥ 0.
 - DZ = 0 on the open set ℝ^P ∖ K_Z, so div_M Z = 0 on M ∖ K_Z. Therefore
 (1.1) ∫_M div_M Z dH^m = 0.
 Now let X ∈ C¹_c(U₀; ℝ^P) and X_k := X * ϕ_{1/k} (standard mollifier). For large k, X_k is C^∞ with support in a fixed compact K' ⊆ U₀, and DX_k → DX uniformly. As H^m(M ∩ K') < ∞ and |div_M Y| ≤ m‖DY‖, (1.1) passes to the limit:
 (1.2) ∫_M div_M X dH^m = 0 for every X ∈ C¹_c(U₀; ℝ^P).
 So V := v(M, 1) is stationary in U₀ (Simon Ch. 2, 5.3 and the definition after 5.4; Ch. 4, 2.6).
2. (Smoothness and zero mean curvature; parent B6.) V = v(M, 1) is a rectifiable m-varifold in U₀ with multiplicity θ ≡ 1, stationary in U₀ by (1.2), so its generalized mean curvature is 0 ∈ L^p for every p. Θ^m(V, y) = 1 at every y ∈ M by (F4). Moreover spt V ∩ U₀ = M: points of M have positive density, and M is relatively closed in U₀.
 By Simon Ch. 5, Theorem 7.1, last part (with N := ℝ^P, which is C^∞, so q is arbitrary), for every y ∈ M and every q there are σ > 0 and a rigid motion after which M ∩ B_σ(y) is the graph of a C^{q+2,α} function. Hence M is a C^∞ embedded submanifold of U₀.
 For C² submanifolds the first variation formula ∫_M div_M X dH^m = −∫_M X·H_M dH^m holds for X ∈ C¹_c(U₀; ℝ^P) (Simon Ch. 2, 4.29–4.30, 5.5(2)). With (1.2) and continuity of H_M, the mean curvature vector H_M vanishes identically.
3. (Unit normal and second fundamental form; parent B7a.)
 - Let a_0, …, a_m be an orthonormal basis of A₀ and Ω(v_0, …, v_m) := det(a_i·v_j)_{i,j=0..m}, an alternating (m+1)-form on ℝ^P. For v ∈ ℝ^P let ι_vΩ be the m-covector (w_1, …, w_m) ↦ Ω(w_1, …, w_m, v).
 - For x ∈ M write ξ(x)(β) = ε_x·β(τ_1, …, τ_m) with τ an orthonormal basis of T_xM and ε_x = ±1. The functional ℓ_x(v) := ξ(x)(ι_vΩ) = ε_x·Ω(τ_1, …, τ_m, v) is linear in v and depends only on ξ(x).
 - ℓ_x vanishes on T_xM, since the m + 1 arguments are then dependent. For a unit vector n ∈ N_x := A₀ ∩ (T_xM)^⊥ (a line, by (0b)), (τ_1, …, τ_m, n) is an orthonormal basis of A₀, so ℓ_x(n) = ±1.
 - Let ν(x) ∈ A₀ be the vector with ν(x)·v = ℓ_x(v) for v ∈ A₀. Then ν(x) ∈ N_x and |ν(x)| = 1.
 - ν is continuous on M, because ξ is continuous and v ↦ ι_vΩ is linear.
 - ν is C^∞: on a smooth chart ψ of M (step 2), n_ψ := the A₀-Riesz representative of v ↦ Ω(∂_1ψ, …, ∂_mψ, v) is smooth and nonzero, ν = ±n_ψ/|n_ψ|, and the sign is locally constant by continuity.
 - For x ∈ M, τ ∈ T_xM: D_τν ⊥ ν (|ν| ≡ 1) and D_τν ∈ A₀, so D_τν ∈ T_xM.
 - The second fundamental form of M (Simon 4.23–4.24) is B_x(τ_i, τ_j) = h_{ij}ν(x) with h_{ij} := −(D_{τ_i}ν)·τ_j = h_{ji}. The normal directions (A₀)^⊥ are constant along M ⊆ A₀ and contribute nothing. Put |A|² := Σ_{i,j} h_{ij}² = Σ_i |D_{τ_i}ν|².
 - |A| is smooth where positive and locally Lipschitz on M.
 - Homogeneity: ν(λx) = ν(x) for λ > 0 (the tangent spaces of the cone are dilation invariant and ν is continuous along rays), so h_{ij}(λx) = λ⁻¹h_{ij}(x) and |A(x)|² = r^{−2}|A(x/|x|)|².
4. (Stability inequality B.1; parent B7b–B7e; Simon 5.4, 5.11, 5.12.) Let ζ ∈ C^∞_c(M) with support K_ζ ⊆ M compact.

 - Finitely many O_{p_k} cover K_ζ. Let φ_k be smooth, compactly supported in O_{p_k}, with Σ_kφ_k = 1 near K_ζ.
 - Put Z := P_{A₀}(Σ_kφ_kY_{p_k}), with P_{A₀} the orthogonal projection onto A₀.
 - On M ∩ O_{p_k}, Y_{p_k} = ζν, so on M, Z = (Σ_kφ_k)·ζν. This equals ζν near K_ζ, and 0 = ζν on M away from K_ζ. Also P_{A₀}ν = ν.
 (4b) Second variation. Let f(t) := H^m(Φ_t^Z(M ∩ K_Z)). By step 1 (applied to this Z), f is C^∞ on (−t₁, t₁), and f(t) ≥ f(0) for |t| < min{t₀(Z), t₁}, so f''(0) ≥ 0. The variation Φ_t^Z = id + tZ has initial velocity Z and acceleration 0. M is C² and stationary in U₀, (closure(M) ∖ M) ∩ U₀ = ∅, and Z|_M = ζν is normal to M. So Lemma 5.11 (from the second variation formula 5.4) gives
 f''(0) = ∫_M (Σ_i |(D_{τ_i}Z)^⊥|² − Σ_{i,j}(Z·B(τ_i, τ_j))²) dH^m.
 - (D_{τ_i}(ζν))^⊥ = (∇_{τ_i}ζ)ν, because D_{τ_i}ν ∈ T_xM (step 3).
 - Z·B(τ_i, τ_j) = ζh_{ij}.
 Hence (Simon 5.12 (‡)) f''(0) = ∫_M (|∇^Mζ|² − |A|²ζ²) dH^m ≥ 0.
 (4c) B.1 holds for every locally Lipschitz ζ with compact support in M. Mollify in finitely many charts (partition of unity) to get ζ_k ∈ C^∞_c(M) with supports in a fixed compact K' ⊆ M, ζ_k → ζ uniformly and ∇^Mζ_k → ∇^Mζ in L²(H^m⌞K'). Here H^m(K') < ∞ and |A| is bounded on K'.

 (5a) Simons' identity B.8 holds:
 ½Δ_M|A|² = Σ_{i,j,k} h²_{ij;k} − |A|⁴ + h_{ij}H_{;ij} + H h_{mi}h_{mj}h_{ij}, with H = h_{kk}.
 Ingredients: h_{ij} = h_{ji} (B.4); Codazzi h_{ij;k} = h_{ik;j} (B.5, the ambient curvature is 0); Gauss R_{ijkl} = h_{il}h_{jk} − h_{ik}h_{jl} (B.6); the commutation formula B.7. Printed proof:

 With H ≡ 0 (step 2): ½Δ_M|A|² = Σ h²_{ij;k} − |A|⁴.
 (5b) Lemma B.11 (cone): where |A| > 0, D := Σ_{i,j,k} h²_{ij;k} − Σ_k |A|^{−2}(Σ_{i,j}h_{ij}h_{ij;k})² ≥ 2r^{−2}|A|². Printed proof:
 - At x ∈ M choose the frame with τ_m = x/|x| radial and τ_1, …, τ_{m−1} constant along the ray ℓ_x (possible by (0b) and homogeneity).
 - Then (1) h_{mj} = h_{jm} = 0 on ℓ_x, since ν is constant along rays, and (2) h_{ij;m} = −r^{−1}h_{ij} on ℓ_x, by h_{ij}(λx) = λ⁻¹h_{ij}(x).

 Since |∇^M|A||² = Σ_k |A|^{−2}(Σ_{ij}h_{ij}h_{ij;k})² where |A| > 0, (5a) and (5b) give there
 (1) ½Δ_M|A|² + |A|⁴ ≥ 2r^{−2}|A|² + |∇_M|A||².
 Where |A| = 0: ∇_M|A| = 0 H^m-a.e. (|A| is locally Lipschitz, and its gradient vanishes a.e. on a level set), and ½Δ_M|A|² = Σh²_{ij;k} ≥ 0. So (1) holds H^m-a.e. on M.
6. (Inequality (3); printed proof of B.2.) Let ψ be locally Lipschitz with compact support in M. Apply B.1 (step 4c) to ζ := |A|ψ:
 (2) ∫_M |A|⁴ψ² ≤ ∫_M |∇(|A|ψ)|² = ∫_M (|∇ψ|²|A|² + ψ²|∇|A||² + 2ψ|A|∇ψ·∇|A|).

 (3) 2∫_M r^{−2}ψ²|A|² dH^m ≤ ∫_M |A|²|∇_Mψ|² dH^m.

 (4) ∫_M r^{−2}ψ²|A|² dH^m < ∞.
 If the right side of (3) is infinite there is nothing to prove; assume it is finite.
 - For 0 < κ < 1 let γ_κ be Lipschitz on ℝ^P with 0 ≤ γ_κ ≤ 1, γ_κ = 1 on {κ ≤ r ≤ κ⁻¹}, γ_κ = 0 on {r ≤ κ/2} ∪ {r ≥ 2κ⁻¹}, linear in r on the two transition annuli, so |∇γ_κ| ≤ 3/r.

 - closure(M) ∩ ∂B_1 = M ∩ ∂B_1, so Σ is closed and bounded;
 - ∂B_1 meets M transversally, since x ∈ T_xM is not tangent to the sphere at x.
 Ψ : (0, ∞) × Σ → M, Ψ(r, σ) := rσ, is a diffeomorphism (cone property; inverse x ↦ (|x|, x/|x|)) with Jacobian r^{m−1} with respect to dr ⊗ H^{m−1}⌞Σ. By the area formula,
 (5) ∫_M f dH^m = ∫_0^∞ r^{m−1}∫_Σ f(rσ) dH^{m−1}(σ) dr for every Borel f ≥ 0 on M.
 Put c_Σ := ∫_Σ |A|² dH^{m−1} < ∞ (|A| is continuous on the compact Σ). Recall |A(x)|² = r^{−2}|A(x/|x|)|² (step 3).
9. (Choice of ψ; printed (6).) Choose ε > 0 with (m/2 − 2 + ε)² < 2 and (1 + ε)² < 2. This is possible exactly because 2 ≤ m ≤ 6; ε := 1/10 works (SimonGMT AppendixB.exists_final_exponent).

 - By (5) and step 8, ∫_M r^{−2}ψ²|A|² = c_Σ(∫_0^1 r^{m−3+2ε} dr + ∫_1^∞ r^{−1−2ε} dr) < ∞, since m − 3 + 2ε > −1. So (4) holds.
 - |∇_M r| = 1 on M (0b), so |∇_Mψ| = (1 + ε)r^ε on {r < 1} and |m/2 − 2 + ε|·r^{1−m/2−ε} on {r > 1}. The set {r = 1} ∩ M = Σ is H^m-null.
 Hence (3) becomes
 (6) 2∫_{M∩{r<1}} |A|²r^{2ε} + 2∫_{M∩{r>1}} |A|²r^{2−m−2ε} ≤ (1 + ε)²∫_{M∩{r<1}} |A|²r^{2ε} + (m/2 − 2 + ε)²∫_{M∩{r>1}} |A|²r^{2−m−2ε},
 with all integrals finite (each is bounded by c_Σ times the convergent integrals above). Since 2 − (1 + ε)² > 0 and 2 − (m/2 − 2 + ε)² > 0, both integrals vanish. |A| is continuous and every nonempty relatively open subset of M has positive H^m-measure (F3), so |A| ≡ 0 on M.

 - |A| ≡ 0 gives D_τν = 0 for every tangent τ (step 3: |A|² = Σ_i|D_{τ_i}ν|²), so ν is locally constant on M. Let M_c be a connected component of M (open in M, M being a manifold) and ν_c the constant value of ν on M_c.
 - For a C¹ curve γ in M_c, (ν_c·γ)' = ν_c·γ' = 0, so ν_c·x = const_c on M_c (connected manifolds are path connected).
 - For x ∈ M_c the ray {tx : t > 0} lies in M (0a), is connected and meets M_c, so it lies in M_c. Letting t ↓ 0 gives const_c = 0. Hence M_c ⊆ H_c := A₀ ∩ ν_c^⊥, an m-dimensional linear subspace.

 - M_c is closed in H_c ∖ {0}: it is closed in M (components are closed), and M is closed in U₀ (0a).

subproblems.title: H^m of a ball in an m-dimensional linear subspace (parent B10c)
subproblems.statement: The m-dimensional Hausdorff measure of a ball in an m-dimensional subspace. Data: P, m ∈ ℕ; a linear subspace H₀ ⊆ ℝ^P with dim H₀ = m (Module.finrank ℝ H₀ = m); ρ > 0. Conclusion: H^m(H₀ ∩ B_ρ(0)) = ω_m·ρ^m, i.e. μHE[m](H₀ ∩ ball 0 ρ) = unitBallVolume m · ofReal(ρ^m), where unitBallVolume m is the Lebesgue measure of the unit ball of ℝ^m.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (H₀ : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), Module.finrank ℝ H₀ = m → ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → μHE[m] ((H₀ : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ ball 0 ρ) = unitBallVolume m * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ m)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Parent step B10c of the supplied proof of codim1_simons_regular_cone_density: "H^m on the m-plane H₀ is m-dimensional Lebesgue measure", so H^m(H₀ ∩ B_ρ(0)) = ω_mρ^m. Book normalization: Simon Ch. 2, §1 and Ch. 3 (H^n = L^n on ℝ^n); here H^m := μHE[m], which equals volume on Euclid m (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume) and is invariant under isometries (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image). ω_m := unitBallVolume m = volume(ball (0 : Euclid m) 1).

Proof. Fix P, m, an m-dimensional linear subspace H₀ ⊆ ℝ^P and ρ > 0.
1. (A linear isometry onto H₀.) H₀ with the inner product of ℝ^P is an m-dimensional inner product space. Fix an orthonormal basis b_1, …, b_m of H₀ (for m = 0 the empty family) and define ι : ℝ^m → ℝ^P by ι(a) := Σ_i a_i b_i. By orthonormality |ι(a) − ι(a')|² = Σ_i (a_i − a'_i)² = |a − a'|². So ι is a linear isometry with range ι = H₀.
2. (The ball.) ι(B_ρ(0)) = H₀ ∩ B_ρ(0). Indeed ι(0) = 0 and |ι(a)| = |a|, so ι maps B_ρ(0) ⊆ ℝ^m into H₀ ∩ B_ρ(0). Conversely every z ∈ H₀ ∩ B_ρ(0) is ι(a) for some a, and |a| = |z| < ρ.
3. (Isometry invariance.) μHE[m] is preserved by isometries: μHE[m](ι(E)) = μHE[m](E) for every E ⊆ ℝ^m. Hence H^m(H₀ ∩ B_ρ(0)) = μHE[m](B_ρ(0) ⊆ ℝ^m).
4. (Lebesgue measure of the ball.) On ℝ^m = Euclid m, μHE[m] = volume. Volume is an additive Haar measure on the m-dimensional space Euclid m, so volume(B_ρ(0)) = ρ^m·volume(B_1(0)) for ρ > 0 (Mathlib Measure.addHaar_ball_of_pos, valid for every ρ > 0 including m = 0, with finrank ℝ (Euclid m) = m). In [0, ∞] this is ofReal(ρ^m)·ω_m.
5. Hence μHE[m](H₀ ∩ ball 0 ρ) = unitBallVolume m · ofReal(ρ^m), by commutativity of multiplication in [0, ∞]. (For m = 0 both sides equal 1: H₀ = {0} and μHE[0]{0} = μH[0]{0} = 1.) ∎
proof_key_steps: An orthonormal basis of H₀ gives a linear isometry ι : ℝ^m → ℝ^P onto H₀ with ι(B_ρ(0)) = H₀ ∩ B_ρ(0).
μHE[m] is invariant under isometries and equals Lebesgue measure on ℝ^m.
The Lebesgue measure of B_ρ(0) ⊆ ℝ^m is ρ^m·ω_m.

Source: step 1 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, §1: coordinate covectors dx^I and the pairing of Λⁿ with Λₙ). The Cauchy–Binet identity is proved inline.
Notation:
- e_0, …, e_{P−1} is the standard basis of ℝ^P (EuclideanSpace.basisFun), and v(i) is the i-th coordinate of v ∈ ℝ^P.
- Λⁿ := Covector (Euclid P) n, the continuous alternating n-linear maps (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ; Λₙ := MultiVector P n = Λⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝ.
- 𝓘 is the finite set of strictly increasing I : Fin n → Fin P, and e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}).
- For α ∈ Λⁿ, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I ∈ 𝓘} α(e_I)²)^{1/2}. The defining sum runs over all I : Fin n → Fin P, with term α(e_I)² for strictly increasing I and 0 otherwise, so it is the same sum.
- For v = (v_0, …, v_{n−1}) ∈ (ℝ^P)^n and I ∈ 𝓘, v^I is the n×n matrix with (k, j) entry v_j(I(k)).
1. (Coordinate covectors.) For I ∈ 𝓘 let dx^I ∈ Λⁿ be dx^I(v) := det(v^I). It is n-linear and alternating in v, because the determinant is multilinear and alternating in its columns and column j, (v_j(I(k)))_k, depends linearly on v_j. It is continuous because ℝ^P is finite-dimensional. In SimonGMT (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter06.FormsDuality), dx^I = wedgeCovectors n (fun k ↦ EuclideanSpace.proj (I k)), and wedgeCovectors_apply_det gives exactly this formula. For n = 0, dx^I is the constant covector 1, the determinant of the empty matrix.
2. (Kronecker property.) For I, J ∈ 𝓘, dx^I(e_J) = 1 if I = J and dx^I(e_J) = 0 if I ≠ J. The matrix (e_J)^I has (k, j) entry 1 if I(k) = J(j) and 0 otherwise. If I = J it is the identity matrix. If I ≠ J, the ranges differ, because a strictly increasing map Fin n → Fin P is the increasing enumeration of its range. Both ranges have n elements, so some I(k) is not in range J. Row k of (e_J)^I is then zero, and the determinant is 0.
3. (Expansion.) For every α ∈ Λⁿ and v ∈ (ℝ^P)^n: α(v) = Σ_{I ∈ 𝓘} α(e_I)·dx^I(v).
 Both sides are alternating n-linear functions of v; the right side is a linear combination of the dx^I. By multilinearity, two n-linear maps on ℝ^P agree once they agree on every basis tuple e_f := (e_{f(0)}, …, e_{f(n−1)}), f : Fin n → Fin P.
 - If f is not injective, both alternating maps vanish at e_f, which has a repeated entry.
 - If f is injective, let J ∈ 𝓘 enumerate range f increasingly, and let σ be the permutation of Fin n with f = J ∘ σ. By alternation, each side at e_f equals sign(σ) times its value at e_J. At e_J the right side is Σ_I α(e_I) dx^I(e_J) = α(e_J) by step 2.
 Hence the two sides agree.
4. (Sum of squared minors; Cauchy–Binet.) For every orthonormal family τ = (τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) in ℝ^P, Σ_{I ∈ 𝓘} det(τ^I)² = 1. This is the Cauchy–Binet formula det(AᵀA) = Σ_I det(A_I)² for the P×n matrix A with columns τ_j, where AᵀA = Id. Self-contained derivation:
 - Let δ_τ ∈ Λⁿ be δ_τ(v) := det(⟨τ_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j}. It is n-linear, alternating and continuous for the same reasons as dx^I, and equals wedgeCovectors n (fun i ↦ ⟨τ_i, ·⟩).
 - By orthonormality, δ_τ(τ) = det(⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩) = det(Id) = 1.
 - δ_τ(e_I) = det(τ_i(I(j)))_{i,j} = det((τ^I)ᵀ) = det(τ^I), and dx^I(τ) = det(τ^I).
 - Step 3 with α = δ_τ and v = τ gives 1 = δ_τ(τ) = Σ_I δ_τ(e_I)·dx^I(τ) = Σ_I det(τ^I)².
5. (Proof of (a).) Let ξ, Q satisfy IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q, with orthonormal τ and sign s, so ξ(α) = s·α(τ) for all α. For α ∈ Λⁿ, step 3 and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality in ℝ^𝓘 give
 |ξ(α)| = |α(τ)| = |Σ_I α(e_I) det(τ^I)| ≤ (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2}·(Σ_I det(τ^I)²)^{1/2} = |α|·1,
 using step 4.
6. (Definition of L.) For ζ ∈ Λₙ put L(ζ) := Σ_{I ∈ 𝓘} ζ(dx^I)·dx^I. Each ζ ↦ ζ(dx^I) is evaluation at a fixed point, a continuous linear functional on Λₙ. So L is a finite sum of continuous linear maps Λₙ → Λⁿ, i.e. L ∈ (MultiVector P n →L[ℝ] Covector (Euclid P) n). For example, L = Σ_I (ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℝ (dx^I)).smulRight (dx^I). L does not depend on ξ.
7. (Coefficients of L(ζ).) For J ∈ 𝓘, step 2 gives L(ζ)(e_J) = Σ_I ζ(dx^I)·dx^I(e_J) = ζ(dx^J). Hence |L(ζ)|² = Σ_{J ∈ 𝓘} ζ(dx^J)².
8. (Proof of (b) and (c).) For ξ as in step 5, ξ(dx^J) = s·dx^J(τ) = s·det(τ^J).
 - By step 7 and step 4, |L(ξ)|² = Σ_J s²·det(τ^J)² = 1, so |L(ξ)| = 1 ≤ 1.
 - By linearity of ξ, ξ(L(ξ)) = Σ_I ξ(dx^I)·ξ(dx^I) = Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1.
9. (Degenerate cases need no separate treatment.)
 - For n = 0, 𝓘 consists of the empty map, e_∅ is the empty tuple, dx^∅ = 1 and |α| = |α(e_∅)|. Steps 1–8 hold verbatim.
 - If n > P, then 𝓘 = ∅ and step 4 would give 0 = 1. So ℝ^P has no orthonormal family of n vectors, the hypothesis IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q never holds, and the statement is vacuous (L = 0).
proof_key_steps: Define dx^I(v) = det(v_j(I(k)))_{k,j} (SimonGMT wedgeCovectors of coordinate projections); dx^I(e_J) = δ_IJ for strictly increasing I, J.
Expansion α(v) = Σ_I α(e_I)·dx^I(v): both sides are alternating multilinear and agree on all basis tuples.
Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1 for orthonormal τ (Cauchy–Binet), by expanding δ_τ(v) = det(⟨τ_i, v_j⟩) at v = τ.
Cauchy–Schwarz gives |ξ(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ |α|.
L(ζ) = Σ_I ζ(dx^I)·dx^I is continuous linear, with |L(ξ)|² = Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1 and ξ(L(ξ)) = Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1.

subproblems.title: Support lemma (Simon 6.2.11): a current vanishes on test forms supported away from its support
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set, S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) with tsupport ω disjoint from spt S, where spt S = U ∖ Z_S and Z_S is the union of all open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and S(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W (GeometricCurrentOn.support). Then S(ω) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note. This child is the accepted declaration Submission.dtc_vanish_off_support of DAG node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.vanish_off_support-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 44ef61f79e21). It is reused with its identical frozen Lean type, so it adds no DAG node. Used by the new child offvertex_rep (step 7): C vanishes on the partition-of-unity piece supported off spt C. The reviewed proof from that node's parent-supplied handoff follows verbatim.

Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.11 (definition of spt T, chapter-06.txt lines 297–301); the partition-of-unity argument below is the standard reason why the union in 2.11 is itself a set on which the current vanishes. Notation: "S vanishes on W" means S(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W.
1. K := tsupport ω is compact and K ⊆ U, because ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) is a compactly supported smooth form with tsupport ω ⊆ U. If K = ∅ then ω = 0 and S(ω) = 0 by linearity; assume K ≠ ∅.
2. Since K ⊆ U and K ∩ spt S = ∅, we have K ⊆ U ∖ spt S ⊆ Z_S. By compactness there are finitely many open sets W₁,…,W_m from the family defining Z_S (each with S vanishing on W_i) such that K ⊆ W₁ ∪ … ∪ W_m.
3. Take a smooth partition of unity on ℝ^P subordinate to the open cover {W₁,…,W_m, ℝ^P ∖ K} (e.g. Mathlib's SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate for the closed set K and the cover by W₁,…,W_m): smooth ψ₁,…,ψ_m : ℝ^P → [0,1] with tsupport ψ_i ⊆ W_i for each i and Σ_i ψ_i(y) = 1 for every y ∈ K.
4. For each i, ψ_iω (pointwise product of a smooth function and a smooth n-form) is smooth, and tsupport(ψ_iω) ⊆ tsupport ψ_i ∩ tsupport ω ⊆ W_i ∩ K; in particular it is compact and contained in U. Thus ψ_iω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport(ψ_iω) ⊆ W_i, and S(ψ_iω) = 0 since S vanishes on W_i.
5. ω = Σ_i ψ_iω pointwise: if ω(y) ≠ 0 then y ∈ K and Σ_iψ_i(y) = 1; if ω(y) = 0 both sides vanish. By linearity of S, S(ω) = Σ_i S(ψ_iω) = 0.
proof_key_steps: tsupport ω is a compact subset of the zero region of S, hence covered by finitely many open sets on which S vanishes.
A smooth partition of unity subordinate to this finite cover splits ω into test forms supported in those sets.
Each piece is annihilated by S; linearity gives S(ω) = 0.

subproblems.title: The cone identity in terms of test forms (parent step 2)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) a cone current (IsConeCurrent C: for every λ > 0 and every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P), currentEval (blowUp C 0 λ) ω = C(ω), where blowUp C 0 λ = η_{0,λ#}C is the proper affine push-forward of C by η(y) = −λ^{-1}·0 + λ^{-1}y). Then for every λ > 0 and every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) there is a test form ω' ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P) with ω'(y) = λ^{-n}·ω(λ^{-1}y) for every y ∈ ℝ^P and C(ω') = C(ω).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), IsConeCurrent C → ∀ lam : ℝ, 0 < lam → ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, ∃ ω' : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, (∀ y, (ω' : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) y = (lam⁻¹ ^ n) • (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (lam⁻¹ • y)) ∧ C ω' = C ω
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note. This child is the accepted declaration Submission.cone_current_apply_dilation_pullback of DAG node root.half_space_cone_lies_in_boundary-a1.cone_measure_homogeneous-a1.cone_pullback_identity-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 52115c22ec2d). It is reused with its identical frozen Lean type, so it adds no DAG node. Used by the new child offvertex_rep (step 3, parent B4): the zero region, hence the support, of a cone current is invariant under dilations. The reviewed proof from that node's parent-supplied handoff follows verbatim.

Source: parent step 2 ("By the contract, blowUp C 0 λ is the push-forward of C by the proper affine map η(y) = −λ^{-1}·0 + λ^{-1}y = S(y), acting by (blowUp C 0 λ)(ω) = C(η^#ω) with (η^#ω)(y) = ω(S(y))∘(λ^{-1}id) = λ^{-n}ω(λ^{-1}y) (affinePullbackForm with L = λ^{-1}id, b = 0); η^#ω is again a test form because η is a proper affine isomorphism. The domain of blowUp C 0 λ is dilation 0 λ '' univ = univ, so every test form ω on ℝ^P satisfies the test-form condition in currentEval, and IsConeCurrent C gives (2.1) C(ω) = C(η^#ω)"). Book: Simon 7.3.1(2) (cone: η_{0,λ#}C = C) and Ch. 6, 2.23 (chapter-06.txt line 408: f_#T(ω) = T(f^#ω)); the cone property is used in the proof of 7.4.5 (chapter-07.txt lines 697–698).

Fix λ > 0 and ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n. Put L := dilationCLM P λ = λ^{-1} · id (a continuous linear map of ℝ^P) and b := −(λ^{-1} · 0), so that dilation 0 λ y = b + L y for all y (definition of dilation), and put V := dilation 0 λ '' univ, the domain of blowUp C 0 λ.

1. IsConeCurrent C, applied to λ, the proof of 0 < λ, and ω, gives currentEval (blowUp C 0 λ) ω = C(ω).

2. V = ℝ^P: every x ∈ ℝ^P equals dilation 0 λ (λx), because −(λ^{-1}·0) + λ^{-1}(λx) = 0 + x = x (λ ≠ 0). Hence tsupport ω ⊆ V. Moreover ω is a test form (smooth with compact support; first component of ω.property). So the condition h : IsTestForm ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ V in the definition of currentEval holds, the 'if' takes its positive branch, and currentEval (blowUp C 0 λ) ω = (blowUp C 0 λ) ⟨ω, h⟩.

3. By the contract's definition, blowUp C 0 λ = (C.restrictDomain h_sub).affinePushforward L b h_proper, where h_sub is the inclusion (y ↦ b + L y)^{-1}(V) ⊆ univ and h_proper the properness of y ↦ b + Ly (both proved inside the definition of blowUp). By GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward_apply and GeometricCurrentOn.restrictDomain_apply (both hold by rfl),
 (blowUp C 0 λ) ⟨ω, h⟩ = C(ω'), where ω' := testFormOnInclusion h_sub n (affinePullbackTestOn L b h_proper V n ⟨ω, h⟩).
 Here ω' is an element of TestFormOn univ n (the SimonGMT constructions affinePullbackTestOn and testFormOnInclusion produce test forms; properness of the affine map is what makes the pulled-back form compactly supported), and its underlying form is (testFormOnInclusion_coe, affinePullbackTestOn_coe, definition of affinePullbackForm)
 ω'(y) = affinePullbackForm L b ω y = (ω(b + L y)).compContinuousLinearMap L for every y ∈ ℝ^P.

4. Combining steps 1–3: C(ω') = (blowUp C 0 λ)⟨ω, h⟩ = currentEval (blowUp C 0 λ) ω = C(ω).

5. Pointwise formula. For every y, b + L y = −(λ^{-1}·0) + λ^{-1}y = λ^{-1}y. Let α := ω(λ^{-1}y), an n-covector, i.e. a continuous alternating n-linear map (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ. For v = (v_1, …, v_n) ∈ (ℝ^P)^n,
 (α.compContinuousLinearMap L)(v) = α(λ^{-1}v_1, …, λ^{-1}v_n) = (∏_{i ∈ Fin n} λ^{-1}) · α(v) = (λ^{-1})^n · α(v),
 by multilinearity (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_smul_univ: f(c_1v_1, …, c_nv_n) = (∏_i c_i) · f(v); the product over Fin n of the constant λ^{-1} is (λ^{-1})^n by Finset.prod_const and card (Fin n) = n). By extensionality in v, α.compContinuousLinearMap L = (λ^{-1})^n • α. Hence ω'(y) = (λ^{-1})^n • ω(λ^{-1} • y) for every y ∈ ℝ^P.

6. By steps 3–5, ω' ∈ TestFormOn univ n satisfies ω'(y) = (λ^{-1})^n • ω(λ^{-1} • y) for all y and C(ω') = C(ω), which is the claim.
proof_key_steps: IsConeCurrent gives currentEval (blowUp C 0 λ) ω = C ω.
dilation 0 λ '' univ = univ, so currentEval takes its test-form branch.
Unfolding blowUp (affinePushforward of restrictDomain) gives C ω' for the test form ω' = affinePullbackForm (λ^{-1}·id) (−λ^{-1}·0) ω.
Multilinearity: α ∘ (λ^{-1}·id) = λ^{-n}α, so ω'(y) = λ^{-n}ω(λ^{-1}y).

subproblems.title: Two unit orientations of the same n-plane differ by a sign
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^P and let v, w ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n: continuous linear functionals on n-covectors, ⟨α, v⟩ = v(α)). If v and w are both unit orientations of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf v Q and IsUnitOrientationOf w Q: for some orthonormal families τ, τ' : Fin n → ℝ^P spanning Q, v(α) = ±α(τ) and w(α) = ±α(τ') for all n-covectors α), then w = v or w = −v.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (v w : MultiVector P n) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), IsUnitOrientationOf v Q → IsUnitOrientationOf w Q → w = v ∨ w = -v
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note. This child is the accepted declaration Submission.rsdic_unitOrientation_eq_or_eq_neg of DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.integer_combination-a1.orientation_sign-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit fe95347baaed). It is reused with its identical frozen Lean type, so it adds no DAG node. Used by the new child offvertex_rep (step 4): two local orientations of the same tangent plane differ by a sign. The reviewed proof from that node's parent-supplied handoff follows verbatim.

Source: the linear-algebra part of step 3 of the parent proof (orthonormal bases of Q differ by an orthogonal matrix of determinant ±1).

1. Unfolding the hypotheses: there are orthonormal families τ, τ' : Fin n → ℝ^P with span(range τ) = Q = span(range τ'), and signs ε, ε' ∈ {1, −1} with v(α) = ε·α(τ) and w(α) = ε'·α(τ') for every n-covector α (continuous alternating n-linear map ℝ^P → ℝ).

2. Each τ_i and τ'_i lies in Q, so τ, τ' may be regarded as families in the inner product space Q, where they are still orthonormal. Since τ is linearly independent and spans Q, dim Q = n; an orthonormal (hence linearly independent) family of n vectors in the n-dimensional space Q spans Q. Hence τ and τ' are orthonormal bases b and b' of Q indexed by Fin n.

3. Let d := det_b(b'), the determinant of the change-of-basis matrix from b to b'. Both bases are orthonormal, so this matrix is orthogonal and d ∈ {1, −1} (Mathlib OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real).

4. Let α be an n-covector and α_Q its restriction to Q (α composed with the inclusion Q → ℝ^P in each slot), an alternating n-linear form on the n-dimensional space Q. Every such form is a multiple of det_b: α_Q = α_Q(b)·det_b (Mathlib AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det). Evaluating at b' gives α(τ') = α_Q(b') = α_Q(b)·det_b(b') = d·α(τ). The number d does not depend on α.

5. Hence for every α: w(α) = ε'·α(τ') = ε'd·α(τ) = (εε'd)·(ε·α(τ)) = s·v(α), where s := εε'd ∈ {1, −1} (using ε² = 1). Therefore w = s·v, i.e. w = v if s = 1 and w = −v if s = −1. For n = 0 the same argument applies (τ = τ' is the empty family, Q = {0}, d = 1). ∎
proof_key_steps: Both orthonormal families spanning Q are orthonormal bases b, b' of Q.
det_b(b') = ±1 because the change-of-basis matrix is orthogonal.
For every n-covector α, α(τ') = det_b(b')·α(τ) since alternating n-forms on Q are multiples of det_b.
Therefore w = (εε'det_b(b'))·v with εε'det_b(b') ∈ {±1}.

subproblems.title: The tangent space of an embedded submanifold is the range of the derivative of any local representation
subproblems.statement: Let ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P be a local representation of N ⊆ ℝ^P in the sense of Simon Ch. 2 §4 (4.1): V ⊆ ℝ^d and W ⊆ ℝ^P open, ψ of class C^r on V with r ≥ 1, ψ injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ N, V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) compact for every compact K ⊆ W, and Dψ(z) injective for every z ∈ V. Then for every v ∈ V the tangent space T_{ψ(v)}N = {γ'(0) : γ ∈ C¹((−1,1); ℝ^P), γ((−1,1)) ⊆ N, γ(0) = ψ(v)} (tangentSpace N (ψ v)) equals the range of Dψ(v).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d r : ℕ) (N W : Set (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid d)) (ψ : Euclid d → Euclid P) (v : Euclid d), 1 ≤ r → IsOpen V → IsOpen W → ContDiffOn ℝ r ψ V → InjOn ψ V → ψ '' V = W ∩ N → (∀ K ⊆ W, IsCompact K → IsCompact (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' K)) → (∀ z ∈ V, Injective (fderiv ℝ ψ z)) → v ∈ V → tangentSpace N (ψ v) = Set.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note. This child is the accepted declaration Submission.chart_tangentSpace_eq_range_fderiv of DAG node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.chart_tangent_space-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit d626082a69a0). It is reused with its identical frozen Lean type, so it adds no DAG node. Used by the new children density_one_local_rep, offvertex_rep, area_comparison and hypercone_plane: tangent spaces of embedded C¹ submanifolds (and of their open pieces) are the ranges of chart derivatives, hence m-dimensional linear subspaces. The reviewed proof from that node's parent-supplied handoff follows verbatim.

Source: Simon Ch. 2 §4 (definition of T_yM for an embedded submanifold, and its identification with Dψ(ℝ^d)); used in steps 3 and 6 of the parent proof.
1. Setup. Put y := ψ(v) ∈ W ∩ N and L := Dψ(v) = fderiv ℝ ψ v; since V is open and r ≥ 1, ψ is differentiable at v with derivative L. L is injective, so (finite dimension) there is c > 0 with |Lh| ≥ c|h| for all h ∈ ℝ^d; range L is a linear subspace, hence closed.
2. range L ⊆ T_yN. Let w = La. If a = 0, the constant curve γ ≡ y works (y ∈ N). Otherwise choose ρ > 0 with closedBall(v, ρ) ⊆ V and κ > 0 with κ|a| < ρ, and let σ(s) := κ·tanh(s/κ), a smooth function with σ(0) = 0, σ'(0) = 1 and |σ(s)| < κ. Put γ(s) := ψ(v + σ(s)a). Then v + σ(s)a ∈ V for all s, so γ is C^r (in particular C¹) on ℝ ⊇ (−1,1), γ(ℝ) ⊆ ψ(V) ⊆ N, γ(0) = y, and γ'(0) = Dψ(v)(σ'(0)a) = La = w. Hence w ∈ T_yN.
3. Embedding property. If z_k ∈ V and ψ(z_k) → y then z_k → v: the set K := {ψ(z_k) : k} ∪ {y} is compact and contained in W, so V ∩ ψ^{-1}(K) is compact and contains every z_k; any cluster point z ∈ V of (z_k) satisfies ψ(z) = y = ψ(v) by continuity, so z = v by injectivity on V; hence z_k → v.
4. T_yN ⊆ range L. Let w ∈ T_yN, witnessed by γ. As γ is continuous at 0 and W is open, there is s_0 ∈ (0,1) with γ(s) ∈ W ∩ N = ψ(V) for |s| < s_0; write γ(s) = ψ(β(s)) with β(s) ∈ V (unique by injectivity). By step 3 (applied along sequences s_k → 0), β(s) → v as s → 0.
5. Write ψ(z) − y = L(z − v) + ρ(z) with |ρ(z)| ≤ η(|z − v|)·|z − v|, η(t) → 0 as t → 0. For |s| small, η(|β(s) − v|) ≤ c/2, hence |γ(s) − y| ≥ c|β(s) − v| − (c/2)|β(s) − v|, i.e. |β(s) − v| ≤ (2/c)|γ(s) − y|. Since γ is differentiable at 0, |γ(s) − y| ≤ C|s| for small |s|; thus |β(s) − v| = O(|s|) and |ρ(β(s))| = o(|s|).
6. Hence (γ(s) − y)/s = L((β(s) − v)/s) + o(1), so the difference quotients lie within o(1) of range L. Letting s → 0, w = γ'(0) belongs to the closure of range L, which is range L. Together with step 2, tangentSpace N (ψ v) = Set.range (fderiv ℝ ψ v).
proof_key_steps: Curves s ↦ ψ(v + σ(s)a) with σ smooth, bounded, σ'(0) = 1 show range Dψ(v) ⊆ T_{ψ(v)}N.
Properness and injectivity make ψ^{-1} continuous at ψ(v) along N ∩ W.
Injectivity of Dψ(v) gives |β(s) − v| = O(|γ(s) − ψ(v)|), so difference quotients of any curve in N lie in range Dψ(v) up to o(1).

subproblems.title: Hausdorff measure of a bi-Lipschitz image of a subset of ℝⁿ
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, χ : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, E ⊆ ℝ^n and real numbers c₁ > 0, c₂ ≥ 0 such that c₁|a − b| ≤ |χ(a) − χ(b)| ≤ c₂|a − b| for all a, b ∈ E. Then c₁ⁿ·Lⁿ(E) ≤ Hⁿ(χ(E)) ≤ c₂ⁿ·Lⁿ(E), where Lⁿ is Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝ^n = Euclid n and Hⁿ = μHE[n] on ℝ^P (all quantities in [0, ∞]).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (χ : Euclid n → Euclid P) (E : Set (Euclid n)) (c₁ c₂ : ℝ), 0 < c₁ → 0 ≤ c₂ → (∀ a ∈ E, ∀ b ∈ E, c₁ * ‖a - b‖ ≤ ‖χ a - χ b‖ ∧ ‖χ a - χ b‖ ≤ c₂ * ‖a - b‖) → ENNReal.ofReal (c₁ ^ n) * volume E ≤ μHE[n] (χ '' E) ∧ μHE[n] (χ '' E) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (c₂ ^ n) * volume E
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note. This child is the accepted declaration Submission.dimred_rpd_bilipschitz_image_measure of DAG node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.regular_point_density-a1.bilipschitz_measure-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 0501e07ced47). It is reused with its identical frozen Lean type, so it adds no DAG node. Used by the new children density_one_local_rep, offvertex_rep and hypercone_plane: positivity of H^m on open pieces of C¹ submanifolds and the density-one squeeze for C¹ graphs. The reviewed proof from that node's parent-supplied handoff follows verbatim.

Source: the measure comparison used in step 4 of the supplied parent proof ("H^n(M ∩ B_s(z)) = ω_n s^n(1 + o(1))"). In this decomposition the graph and area-formula computation of step 4 is replaced by a bi-Lipschitz squeeze, and this lemma is the measure-theoretic half of it.
Notation. μH[d] is Mathlib's Hausdorff measure. By definition (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def), μHE[n] = c·μH[n] on every metric space, with the same constant c := addHaarScalarFactor(volume on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μH[n]) ∈ [0, ∞). On ℝ^n itself, μHE[n] = volume (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
1. (Upper bound.) By hypothesis, χ is c₂-Lipschitz on E (LipschitzOnWith.of_dist_le_mul). By the Lipschitz image inequality for Hausdorff measures (LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le with d = n ≥ 0), μH[n](χ(E)) ≤ c₂ⁿ·μH[n](E). Multiplying by c gives μHE[n](χ(E)) ≤ c₂ⁿ·μHE[n](E) = c₂ⁿ·volume(E). Here c₂ⁿ = ofReal(c₂ⁿ) = (toNNReal c₂)^(n : ℝ) in [0, ∞].
2. (χ is injective on E.) If a, b ∈ E and χ(a) = χ(b), then c₁|a − b| ≤ 0. Since c₁ > 0, this forces a = b.
3. (Lower bound.) Let g := invFunOn χ E. By step 2, g(χ(a)) = a for all a ∈ E (InjOn.leftInvOn_invFunOn). Hence g maps χ(E) onto E (LeftInvOn.image_image). Multiply by c and by c₁ⁿ ∈ (0, ∞): c₁ⁿ·volume(E) = c₁ⁿ·μHE[n](E) ≤ μHE[n](χ(E)).
